module8: Capstone: audit people and pay data and coach others
Put all seven parts together. You check one team's records from person to payout, then teach another person how to keep them right.
Trace a worker from record to roster, pay input and review.
Check that approved hours, rates and payouts match the records.
Look for fairness, privacy and access problems.
Coach a colleague to repeat the checks every month.
An audit finds a payout total that is 40 hours higher than approved time because late hours were added by hand. You remove them and add a cut-off rule.
Audit a practice team of ten people. Write a one-page report with five findings and give a 15-minute coaching session to a colleague.
Match pay totals to approved records, report five findings with owners, and show that the colleague can repeat two checks alone.
quiz: A worker changes job and manager. What should happen in one step in a good people system?
The people record updates the job, the manager and the access rights together. This avoids old access staying behind and keeps reports correct.
Why keep only the personal data that you need for the job?
Less data means less risk if there is a mistake or a leak, and it follows privacy rules. If you do not need a detail to do the work, do not collect it.
A level 3 technician needs five skills but has three. What does a skills ladder show you?
It shows a gap of two skills. You can then plan learning or practice for those two skills and record proof when they are done.
Two people want to swap shifts. Who needs to approve and why?
Both people agree, and the supervisor approves, so cover and rest rules are still met. A swap with no approval can leave a gap or break a rule.
A worker has 12 days of leave and asks for 15 days. What do you check?
Check the leave balance and policy, then refuse or ask for a different type of leave. Never let the balance go negative without a written rule.
Hours must be approved by Friday for the pay run. A worker's hours arrive on Monday. What happens?
The late hours are not in this run and roll into the next one. A clear cut-off keeps pay fair and the totals easy to check.
In your capstone audit, the payout file totals 1,200 hours but approved time is 1,160 hours. What is your next step?
Do not release the payout. Find the 40 extra hours, compare them to approved records, correct or remove them, and re-check the totals match.
A manager gives a low rating without any notes. How does a good review process respond?
It asks for evidence attached to every rating. A calibration step then checks that ratings are fair across teams and free from bias.
A plan shows 12 technicians will retire in two years. Name two actions.
Start training or hiring to fill the skills, and capture the knowledge of the experienced people. Set dates and owners for each action.
Your yearly access review finds 15 accounts of people who left. What do you do and record?
Remove the accounts, note the date and who approved, and look for why they were missed. Then fix the leaver step so it does not happen again.
ladder: L1 Basic: Know the records
Remember what a people record holds and which details are needed. You can find a person, job and manager in the system.
Show one practice record and ask learners to name each part. Common mistake: collecting details nobody needs.
L2 Awareness: See the whole cycle
Understand how a person moves from hiring to roster, time, pay and review. You can explain in simple words why each record matters.
Draw the cycle and ask where mistakes would spread. Check they know that pay depends on earlier steps.
L3 Foundation: Do routine tasks
Apply the steps to add a person, set a role, build a roster and approve leave. You follow rules for rest, balance and approval.
Give a small team and a week to plan. Common mistake: ignoring rest rules to fill a gap.
L4 Practitioner: Prepare pay inputs
Analyse approved hours, rates and deductions to build a pay input file. You check that totals match the approved records before release.
Plant a few errors in the file and see if learners find them. Check they never release without a reconciliation.
L5 Specialist: Run fair reviews and plans
Evaluate goals, feedback and ratings for evidence and fairness. You also read headcount and turnover to plan the next steps.
Ask learners to defend one rating using evidence only. Common mistake: letting one recent event shape the whole rating.
L6 Advanced: Protect and improve
Create a compliance pack with a retention table, access reviews and change control. You set dates and owners so checks really happen.
Review the pack for dates, owners and a real example. Look for rules that are written but never checked.
L7 Super expert: Audit and coach
Evaluate people and pay data across a team, rank the risks and create a fix plan. You can coach others to run the same checks each month.
Have the learner audit a sample team and coach back. Check for clear findings, fair tone and respect for privacy.
